notes: G02: the suffixed article in the nominative singular, met first on second mention (Nú kemur maður … Maðurinn er Bjarni) and on things already known (konungurinn, presturinn, skotthúfan).

Ásta's problem changed from sweeping the yard (design §6 row 2) to dressing up in her new skotthúfa and waiting on the home field: sópa is not a licensed verb before G04, and the cap is the one Siggi cuts in Kafli 15.
Óðinn is linked to Sleipnir by „Óðinn situr á Sleipni“ (á + dat. of place, glossed Sleipni ← Sleipnir) instead of the genitive hestur Óðins (G10).
Added place chunk í Reykjavík (glossed by the Kafli 1 map); Kemur hann á Jökuldal? is the direction reading of the same string (supported use).
segir það / Afi segir það líka: accusative það, identical in form to the nominative (supported use before G05).
Incidental verbs added: stendur, fer, liggur (9 of 13 used by the end of Kafli 2).

cover.alt: Evening at Hamrar: the household comes home from church. Bjarni rides into the yard first on a big brown horse; behind him Guðrún and Helga on horses, little Ásta riding in front of Guðrún; the farmhand Óli and the maid Þórunn on foot. Siggi stands on the home field waving, afi beside him; Snati barks.
cover.art_brief: Evening of Sunday 2 August 1874, golden low light from the north-west, the valley in shadow. The yard (hlað) and home field of the turf farm Hamrar with its wooden gables. Arriving along the track from down the valley: first Bjarni (44, broad, dark beard, Sunday dark coat and hat) on a big brown Icelandic horse; then Guðrún (38, dark peysuföt with a black skotthúfa) on a grey horse with little Ásta (6, round face, fair plaits) sitting in front of her; Helga (18, tall, light-brown hair in plaits, dark Sunday dress and skotthúfa) on a dun horse; on foot behind, Óli (24, big, red-cheeked, grinning, cap pushed back) and Þórunn (36, thin, dark shawl). Foreground: Siggi on the home field (bandaged foot) waving, toy horse in hand; afi standing beside him; Snati standing and barking. Recognisable from the character sheets; no text.

inference_aids.alt: A skotthúfa: a small flat black knitted cap whose tail ends in a short silver tube with a long black tassel.

Little Ásta in her new black tasselled cap stands very straight on the home field, looking down the empty valley track; Snati sits beside her and a ewe wanders up; behind, at the house, Óli is laughing and Þórunn has her hand over her mouth.
inference_aids.art_brief: Same evening, a little later, the sun lower. Ásta (6) stands alone and very straight in the middle of the home field, hands folded, wearing her best dark dress and a NEW small black knitted skotthúfa with a long tail, a shiny silver tassel holder and a black silk tassel; she gazes solemnly down the empty track along the valley. Snati sits beside her; a curious ewe has come up to her. Background at the farmhouse door: Óli doubled up laughing, Þórunn coming towards Ásta with one hand over her mouth, trying not to laugh. Gentle comedy, never mocking. Same style; no text.

words_with_history.title: Orð með sögu
text: Fjölskylda: afi, pabbi, mamma, Helga, Siggi og Ásta.
Heimili: fjölskylda — og Óli, Þórunn og Snati líka.
words_with_history.note_en: In 1874 a farm household (heimili) counted everyone under one roof: the family, the hired servants (vinnumaður, vinnukona), paupers boarded by the parish and guests. Fjölskylda is the kin; heimili is the household. Servants were hired by the year and changed farms on 14 May.

grammar.title: maður → maðurinn

tables.caption: Nú kemur maður. Maðurinn er Bjarni.
hver? · hvað?
rows: Hvað er þetta? — Þetta er skotthúfa.
Hver er Óðinn? — Það er saga.

grammar.note_en: Icelandic has no word for “a”: hestur is “a horse”. “The” is an ending: hestur-inn, kona-n, barn-ið (kk. -inn, kvk. -in, after -a just -n, hk. -ið). A noun takes it when we already know which one: Nú kemur maður. Maðurinn er Bjarni. Saying what someone is takes none: Ásta er barn. Hver? asks about people, hvað? about things; þessi (this) stands before the noun.
